newsitem.title: UK: Lanica Trust seen eyeing Co-op.
newsitem.headline: Lanica Trust seen eyeing Co-op.

text.p: Lanica Trust Plc is expected to make a 500 million pounds ($820.1 million) offer for the non-food businesses owned by Britain's Co-Operative movement, the Sunday Times reported.

It said the businesses covered by the proposed buyout of Co-Operative Retail and Co-Operative Wholesale societies ranged from petrol stations, funeral parlours, chemists, opticians and department stores.

The newspaper said Lanica's bankers would be writing to the boards of the two Co-Operative companies to inform them of the plans and that an announcement was also likely to be made to the London Stock Exchange.

Lanica was previously known as New Guernsey Securities and changed its name when entrepreneur Andrew Regan took control last year when the stock was trading at 203p. The shares closed on Friday at 16.37 pounds. ($1=.6097 Pound)
